# Tally Health (epigenetic age testing + longevity supplements, founded w/ David Sinclair)

URL: https://tallyhealth.com/

## Type system
- Display/body: `Generator, sans-serif` — a single custom-named grotesk used
  across every level: H1 70px/300 (light), H2 34px/400, body 16px/400. No
  serif or mono; hierarchy comes entirely from size/weight/colour, not a
  font pairing.

## Color system
- bg: cream/off-white `#FAF9F2`, `#F3F4EB`, `#E9E8E4` for light sections.
- **Signature accent**: a magenta-to-coral gradient family — deep plum
  `#4A0C33`/`#731445` as dark surfaces, hot pink `#D93359` and coral-orange
  blended in gradient sections. This is the most saturated, boldest colour
  system in the whole dataset — a hot magenta/burgundy duotone rather than
  clinical blue or spa neutrals.
- text on dark: white; text on cream: deep plum `#4A0C33`.
- Black used only for footer/utility chrome.

## Layout & grid
- Alternates cream and full-bleed saturated-magenta-gradient sections in a
  strict rhythm — roughly every other section flips from light to
  intensely coloured, giving the page a much faster visual pace than any
  other site in the set.
- Centred ~1100px column; the signature "epigenetic age" data
  visualization breaks out to a wide, centred illustrative panel.

## Sections (order observed)
1. Light cream hero: "Unlock more healthy years," product photo (test kit
   on a marble surface), two CTAs (Add-On Supplements / Discover TallyAge)
2. Press logo bar (Fast Company, Forbes, Vogue, Fortune, Bloomberg)
3. "A daily dose of longevity" — magenta gradient section, supplement
   product photography, founder-credibility photo (labelled "Precision
   Longevity")
4. "Your starting point for change" — deep plum section: "How are you
   really aging?" copy + TallyAge test CTA
5. **Signature data visualization**: dark plum/burgundy radial section
   with a circular dot-ring diagram and a large number — "Lower your
   epigenetic age... 43 ↓" — the biological-age reveal as its own full
   hero-scale section
6. "Build your longevity roadmap" — numbered 3-step vertical list
   (01 Pro-longevity formulations, 02 Epigenetic testing, 03 Personalized
   insights) over the same dark gradient
7. "Go all-in with Membership" — light section, feature list
8. Stat callout: "After 6 months, over 62% of Tally Members lower their
   epigenetic age by an average of 2+ years"
9. Testimonial star-rated quote cards (3-up)
10. "Talk Science to Me" — newsletter/contact form on cream
11. Dark plum footer

## Components/signature
- The circular dot-ring "epigenetic age" diagram with a single large
  number and a down-arrow is the standout signature device in the entire
  dataset — it visualizes a single biological-age score as a radial/clock
  metaphor rather than a bar chart or gauge, given a full-bleed dramatic
  section of its own rather than being embedded in a small card.
- Saturated magenta/plum gradient sections used as full section
  backgrounds (not just accents) — most colour-forward site in the set.

## Motion/interactions
- The dot-ring diagram likely animates the number counting down (implied
  by "↓" and the framing "lower your epigenetic age") — a satisfying
  micro-interaction tied directly to the product's core promise.

## Biomarker/trust presentation
- Biological/epigenetic age is the single hero metric, visualized as a
  radial dot-ring with one large number — the clearest example in the
  dataset of "one number, one dramatic visualization" rather than a dense
  multi-biomarker table.
- Trust signals: press logos (Forbes, Vogue, Fortune, Bloomberg), a named
  scientific founder credibility photo/callout, and an aggregate outcome
  stat ("62% of members lower epigenetic age by 2+ years") rather than
  individual clinician bios.
- No visible medical disclaimer copy on the homepage (supplement +
  consumer-test positioning, not a clinic).

## What works
- Proves a longevity-science brand can use loud, fashion-adjacent colour
  (hot magenta/burgundy) instead of clinical blue or spa neutrals, while
  still being taken seriously — the Fast Company/Vogue/Forbes press wall
  does real credibility work to offset the boldness.
- Turning a single biomarker (epigenetic/biological age) into one
  dramatic, full-section visual moment is more memorable than embedding
  the same number in a dashboard card.

## Avoid
- The light-weight (300) Generator sans at 70px on a saturated magenta
  background needs careful contrast checking — legibility is more fragile
  here than on neutral backgrounds.
- Full-bleed saturated-gradient sections back-to-back can fatigue if
  overused; the light-cream sections in between are doing real pacing
  work — don't drop them.

## How to apply
- If the product's core promise reduces to a single number (a score, an
  age, a percentile), give that number its own full-bleed dramatic
  section with a radial/circular visual rather than burying it in a card.
- Use one saturated, non-clinical accent colour (magenta, coral, chartreuse
  — not blue/green) as full section backgrounds, alternated with neutral
  cream sections for pacing, to differentiate from the clinical-blue
  category default.
